subject: Advice on running complex model that yields a not positive definite warning

messages.author: bc08cfd7e1504b0d
messages.subject: Advice on running complex model that yields a not positive definite warning
parts:
I am trying to test a complex CFA model as follows;

 

I have run an initial overall model however it yields the following warning 

Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some cases are empty and will be removed:
  1008
3: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
4: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

 

However it does then say ‘lavaan (0.5-20) converged normally after 277 iterations’

Can anyone help with the following?

  1.  As it converges after 277 iterations does it mean that I can ignore the not positive definite warning and report the findings?

     

    Or

  2.  Has the model has been mispecified

    rq.1<- '

# Measurement part

# expectations

expectations =~ Q24 + Q26 + Q28 + Q32 + Q36

#STV

intrinsic =~ Q21 + Q30

attainment =~ Q25 + Q31 + Q37

STV =~ intrinsic + attainment

SES =~ momed + daded + ISEImo + ISEIfa + books + homepossessions

# Structural part

Aveexampointscore ~ expectations + STV + SES + girl + school

STV ~ SES + girl + school

expectations ~ SES + girl + school'

 

fit <- sem(rq.1, data = mydata, missing='fiml', estimator='MLR')

summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

inspect(fit, 'r2')

inspect(fit,'cor.lv')

Or

  1. Is it due to collinearity (as between attainment value and STV in the correlation matrix).

     

> inspect(fit,'cor.lv')
             expctt intrns attnmn STV   SES  
expectations 1.000                           
intrinsic    0.007  1.000                    
attainment   0.016  0.549  1.000             
STV          0.014  0.496  1.107  1.000      
SES          0.291  0.061  0.137  0.124 1.000

 

And if this is the case in the overall model why does this not occur when testing individual models (e.g.  a model of just STV and achievement)?

 

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Many thanks

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Advice on running complex model that yields a not positive definite warning
parts:
The warning is about an aspect of your results. That aspect is still there. It is (probably) an unexpected result. Therefore, you should not ignore it. A correlation between factors that is beyond 1 could be driven by random sampling error, but many people will take it as a sign of an error in the model.
     You should start by addressing the first message, about a difference in the scaling of observed variables in the model. Such a difference can cause factor-based SEM software to misbehave. This could be the reason why your results includes the unexpected results. You should look at the variances of your observed variables, and make the different variances more similar. If variable A has a variance in the hundreds, while variable B has a variance in the single digits, you can bring them into line by, say, dividing variable A by 10 (the square root of 100). I recommend that you divide by constants, rather than just standardizing the data. Dividing by constants will eliminate the problem without inducing statistical complications.

You should do this before you run lavaan. In R, you can type:

mydata$ISEImo2 <- mydata$ISEImo / 10

and then use 'ISEImo2' in your model instead of 'ISEImo'

parts:
Dear Yves

Thank you so much for the reply, it was most useful and allowed me to scale.

Sadly this did not solve the original problem of the negative variances and non-convergence but was good to investigate. It did converge after 133 rather than 277 iterations but still with the error warnings.

Before I conclude that I have a theoretical model that does not fit the data is there anything else anyone would recommend I try? I believe the model is identified correctly, have removed collinear variables to no avail, there are no errors in the data set and that it has not been mis-specified - largely as it is based on a theoretical model but also because I have successfully run individual models on various parts of the overall model. These yielded similar estimates to the ones showing on the output of these 'improper solutions' in almost all cases.

However as I am new to this I may be missing something else obvious

Many thanks

Matt
